about.title: Watsonville Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Watsonville households rely on everyday products — from farm equipment used along Green Valley Road's agricultural stretches to appliances, tools, and vehicle parts used around town. When one of those products fails because of a design flaw, a manufacturing defect, or a missing warning, the resulting injury can be serious and unexpected. California law allows injured people to pursue claims against manufacturers, distributors, and retailers without having to prove anyone was careless — the focus is on whether the product itself was defective and whether that defect caused harm. We handle defective-product claims directly across Santa Cruz County and work on contingency, meaning there's no upfront cost. If you were hurt by a product, keeping it in its post-injury condition can matter, and getting guidance early can help protect that opportunity.

Traumatic injuries from failed vehicle components

Fall injuries caused by structurally defective products

items.title: Strict Liability Can Simplify Your Path Forward
items.desc: Because California often applies strict liability to defective products, you generally don't need to prove the manufacturer was negligent — just that the product was defective and caused your injury.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the pool of parties available to pursue a claim against.

items.title: Preserving the Product Matters
items.desc: We can advise you on safely keeping the product in its post-injury state, since it often serves as key evidence in a defect claim.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California's strict liability approach, you generally only need to show the product was defective and that the defect caused your injury. This differs from many other injury claims where negligence must be proven.

items.question: I was hurt by farm equipment near Green Valley Road — does that count as a product liability case?
items.answer: It can, depending on whether the equipment had a design, manufacturing, or warning defect. Our team can review the specifics of what happened and how the equipment failed to determine the right legal path.

items.question: What should I do with the product that injured me?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in right after the injury, without repairing or discarding it. This preservation can be important for any later evaluation of the defect.

items.question: Do you charge anything for this service?
items.answer: No. Our team typically works on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation.
